summary.headline: The Affordable Housing Trust voted to reappoint its CPC representative and discussed pursuing state technical assistance grants and zoning updates.
summary.summary: The Affordable Housing Trust discussed revisions to the town 55-plus housing bylaw and determined the proposal would likely target Spring Town Meeting rather than the fall. Members agreed to apply for Massachusetts Housing Partnership Mini-Boost grant funds to assist with financing options and strategic planning. The Trust also discussed exploring a local real estate transfer fee home rule petition and reviewed outreach options before voting to enter executive session to discuss property acquisition.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board conducted roll call attendance and reviewed multiple sets of past minutes. Members approved open session minutes from May 22, 2026, and executive session minutes from May 22, June 12, and June 18, 2026.
key_details: Approved open session minutes of May 22, 2026.
Approved and retained executive session minutes of May 22, June 12, and June 18, 2026.
Clarified lot references and open session exit language in past minutes.

topics.title: Appointment of representative to Community Preservation Committee
topics.summary: The trust discussed the expiration of its representative appointment to the Community Preservation Committee. Ellen Marya agreed to continue serving in the role.
key_details: Ellen Marya has served as the Trust representative to the CPC to date.
The board voted unanimously to reappoint her to the seat.
topics.outcome: Ellen Marya reappointed as CPC representative.

topics.title: 55-plus housing bylaw update
topics.summary: Members reviewed progress on updating the zoning bylaw for 55-plus housing, specifically efforts to remove the existing cap on such developments. Due to timing and the complexity of definitions around affordability and unit inclusion, the Trust plans to collaborate with the Planning Board and town counsel to bring the proposal to Annual Town Meeting in the spring rather than the fall special meeting.
key_details: Proposal stems from recommendations in the housing production plan.
Effort seeks to remove the existing cap on 55-plus housing units in the zoning bylaw.
Trust members plan to consult town counsel regarding bylaw language.
Target timeline shifted to Spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting.
topics.outcome: Discussion held; board members will consult with town counsel and the Planning Board.

topics.title: Financing approaches and technical assistance grants
topics.summary: The Trust evaluated grant and assistance opportunities through the Massachusetts Housing Partnership, specifically the Mini-Boost technical assistance program offering up to $5,000. Members decided to prepare applications focusing on board strategic planning and municipal housing financing models. A member also volunteered to review the inventory of town-owned parcels for affordable housing potential.
key_details: MHP Mini-Boost program offers between $2,000 and $5,000 in consultant assistance.
David Joyner will lead the application for the housing finance technical assistance.
The chair will lead the application for the goals and strategy planning assistance.
A member will re-examine town-owned land parcels, including land near Coslin Drive and Dell/EMC property.
topics.outcome: Members agreed to submit applications for MHP Mini-Boost technical assistance.

topics.title: Real estate transfer fee and community engagement
topics.summary: A member proposed exploring a local real estate transfer fee of 0.5% to 2% on higher-value property sales, similar to special acts pursued in communities like Concord and Nantucket, to fund the housing trust. The Trust debated whether town meeting would support such a fee and discussed broader public engagement methods, such as adding housing questions to the Municipal Technology Committee survey.
key_details: Proposal suggested fees between 0.5% and 2% on property transactions over a set threshold like $1.5 million.
Enacting a fee would require Town Meeting approval and a special act from the state legislature.
Members discussed potential pushback from sellers and the need for early public outreach.
The Trust will look into adding questions to an upcoming municipal survey and coordinating with regional planning partners.
topics.outcome: Discussion held; no formal action taken.

topics.title: CHAPA Housing Leadership Academy update
topics.summary: Ellen Marya provided an update on her participation in the Citizens Housing and Planning Association Housing Leadership Academy. Participants in the six-month program complete a housing policy or zoning project, and she invited suggestions from Trust members.
key_details: Program includes approximately 30 municipal officials from across Massachusetts.
Participants will select and complete an affordable housing project by late summer or fall.

topics.title: Executive session for property acquisition
topics.summary: The Trust voted to adjourn into executive session under state open meeting law exemption 6 to discuss the potential acquisition of real property.
key_details: Invoked Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 30A, Section 21(a)(6).
The chair declared that open discussion would be detrimental to the town negotiating position.
The Trust did not return to open session.

votes.motion: Reappoint Ellen Marya as the Affordable Housing Trust representative to the Community Preservation Committee
Enter executive session under MGL Chapter 30A, Section 21(a)(6) to discuss potential property acquisition and not reconvene in open session

upcoming.what: Submit applications for Massachusetts Housing Partnership Mini-Boost technical assistance
Finalize 55-plus housing bylaw revision proposal for Town Meeting
